TT-003.scientific_review: Focal primary full text and source-location record checked: twelve outdoor tanks, four per treatment; all received fish before fluoxetine treatments. Zooplankton abundance rebounded less after fish removal in drug-exposed tanks while dosing continued throughout all 21 post-removal days. Tank variability, unresolved mechanism and tank-to-lake limit retained. No claim of recovery after drug withdrawal, permanent damage or fish-only initial causation. Independent context checked against Schultz et al. 2010 USGS research record (effluent-associated antidepressant detection) and Ekvall et al. 2014 full text (zooplankton grazers and fish food-web relationships). These context papers do not establish the focal mechanism. Reference-media rights and credits retained.

TT-003.narrative_review: The complete 66-second story opens with a predator-removal recovery puzzle, identifies zooplankton and their food-web role early, introduces independently sourced wastewater context, then asks whether a second pressure changes recovery. The tank experiment answers that question in a bounded setting. Continued dosing is the narrative pivot: one pressure ended while another remained. Variability and unresolved mechanism prevent a false neat resolution; the ending returns to the restoration question and explicitly distinguishes experimental communities from lakes. Context supports the story rather than merely padding methods/results. No invented interviews, quotes, researcher emotions or universal management prescription.
